To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we study transport of noninteracting electrons through two double quantum dot systems embedded in an Aharono-Bohm interferometric structure and that the system exhibits a magnetic flux-induced negative conductance region.

(i) we study the transport of non-interaction electrons through two quantum-dot molecules embedded in an AB interferometer; (ii) in equilibrium, the system exhibits bound states in continuum and total transmission suppression; (iii) it also shows a magnetic-field dependent effective level attraction and line of perfect transmission when intramolecular coupling are weak; (iv) out of equilibrium, the currents display two kind of NDC regions, which have two different origins: one is generated by the NDC arising
the magnetic flux induces negative differential conductance and level attraction in two double quantum dots embedded in an Ahronov-Bohm intereferometer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport properties of a double-quantum-dot molecule embedded in an Ahronov-Bohm (AB) ring.
transport properties of non-interacting particles through a double quantum dot molecule embedded in an Ahronov-Bohm (AB) interferometer.

the study of the transport properties of non-interacting particles through a double-quantum dot molecule embedded in an Ahronov-Bohm (AB) interferometer, and the effects of the magnetic flux on the transport properties of the system are analyzed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system displays a rich and interesting physics, which can be tuned by the magnetic flux and the intramolecular tunneling.
the magnetic flux can be a very effective parameter to tune the electronic transport in a two quantum dot molecule.
the system under study is a very rich one, with several different mechanisms of NDC and BIC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system exhibits a rich phenomenology that includes BIC, NDC and perfect transmission, and that the magnetic flux plays a fundamental role in the generation of the latter two.
the magnetic flux is a powerful tool to manipulate the transport through a quantum dot system, and it is also a very useful tool to control the transport through a double quantum dot molecule.
the magnetic field can be used to tune the system from a regime of strong level repulsion to another one of strong level attraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic flux can be used as a knob to control the transport in quantum dot interferometers, which is of relevance for the design of quantum devices.
the Aharonov- Bohm ring provides an efficient mechanism to control the transport of electrons in quantum dot molecules.
, by using an AharonovBohm ring with embedded quantum dot molecules, one can tune the effective level attraction and generate NDC regions at small voltages.
